first_impression.reaction: Googled 'honeymoon planner vs travel agent' expecting the usual 'planners are magic, agents are order-takers' pitch. Instead the intro says the labels don't mean anything official and to compare the service. Fine, I'd rather that than a made-up distinction. Went to the FAQ first: it says I don't need an agent at all. A business that sells planning telling me that is a point in its favour. The paid-how section asks the commission question I'd ask. Where it lets me down is the table, where both columns say the same thing, and the Wedded Wonderland bit, which tells me to ask about supplier payments and then doesn't say anything about its own.

journey.quote: In practice both are labels rather than defined titles, and many businesses use more than one of them.
journey.reaction: Good. I'll check that against other sites, but it's the honest starting point. No pretending there's an official difference.

journey.quote: So compare the service, not the title.
journey.reaction: I searched 'vs' and I'm not getting a winner. Slightly annoying, but it's a fair answer. I'll take questions over a sales pitch.

journey.quote: No. Consumer guarantees apply whether you book directly or through an agent or intermediary.
journey.reaction: Read the FAQ first, as always. A one-word 'No' from a business that sells this service. That's the most credible line on the page.

journey.section: Start with the questions you ask yourselves
journey.quote: Some couples love comparing rooms late at night; others want to describe a feeling and receive a finished itinerary.
journey.reaction: Bit of mood writing. I'm the 'comparing rooms late at night' one. Harmless, I skimmed past it.

journey.section: The same questions, side by side
journey.quote: | Ask a planner | Ask an agent | Why it matters |
journey.reaction: Two columns, word-for-word identical in every row. I scanned across looking for the difference and there isn't one. I get the point (ask everyone the same thing), but a table built like this looks like it's meant to compare and then doesn't. One column would do.

journey.section: The same questions, side by side
journey.quote: Do you receive anything from suppliers, and is that disclosed?
journey.reaction: That's my question. 'Anything' is broader than just commission, which I like.

journey.section: Questions about how they are paid
journey.quote: Do you earn commission from the places you book, and is that shown to us?
journey.reaction: Good, but there's still nothing about mark-ups or asking to see the supplier's own price. 'No commission' and 'no mark-up' aren't the same answer.

journey.section: Questions about what happens when plans change
journey.quote: An agent or intermediary is usually bound by the provider's terms and, legally, may only need to pass on the remedy that provider offers.
journey.reaction: That's the catch with going through a middleman, and they've said it out loud. Linked to the ACCC too. Exactly what I want.

journey.section: What does our travel insurance need to cover?
journey.quote: Insolvency insurance is not compulsory for agents, so ask whoever you book through whether they hold it.
journey.reaction: After my last vendor this is the one I care about. Useful, and it's advice against their own industry.

journey.quote: Our view, set out on our Wedded Concierge page, is that for a destination wedding you need both, working as one.
journey.reaction: Funny how the answer is exactly what they sell. At least they label it 'our view' and it comes after the neutral stuff, not before.

journey.quote: Wedded Wonderland is both in one relationship, so you never have to explain your wedding to someone who has not planned it, or your travel to someone who has not moved guests overseas.
journey.reaction: 'Never' is a sales word. Nothing on the page shows me how many weddings or guest moves they've done.

journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Good, that's the minimum. But two sections ago they told me to ask whether a business receives anything from suppliers. Their own bullet list skips that question entirely. They didn't claim to answer it, so it's not a lie, but I noticed the gap.

journey.quote: We plan venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: Big claim, no evidence on the page. I'd check it.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Wonderland fee worked out: flat, percentage of the trip, per booking or a mix? (deferred business detail)
Do you receive commissions or add mark-ups on the suppliers your Advisor books, and will you disclose which? You tell me to ask, so I'm asking. (deferred business detail)
Even a rough range: what have couples actually paid you for honeymoon-only planning? (deferred business detail)
Show me a real honeymoon you've planned, ideally one following a destination wedding, with the fee and trip cost shown separately. (deferred business detail)
Do you hold insolvency insurance? (deferred business detail)
Are there any perks or extras through you that I couldn't get booking direct, and are they itemised? (deferred business detail)
Who books the honeymoon in practice: do you hold the bookings, or do they sit in our names with the supplier? (deferred business detail)
Who do we call while we're away, and at what hours? The page tells me to ask this of everyone but doesn't answer it for you. (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: | Ask a planner | Ask an agent | Why it matters |
turn_offs_found.why: The two columns are identical in every row. It looks like a comparison and isn't one, which wastes my time scanning for a difference that doesn't exist.

turn_offs_found.quote: Wedded Wonderland is both in one relationship, so you never have to explain your wedding to someone who has not planned it, or your travel to someone who has not moved guests overseas.
turn_offs_found.why: Absolute 'never' with no evidence behind it. Reads like marketing on a page that otherwise sticks to sourced facts.

turn_offs_found.quote: We plan venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
turn_offs_found.why: Sweeping claim with nothing to back it on the page. Mild, but it stands out against the sourced material.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the 'Questions about how they are paid' list, as columns for our planner comparison spreadsheet
Our Reddit thread, the insolvency and 'agent may only need to pass on the remedy' points

cta_reaction.quote: Tell your Wedded Advisor about the wedding, the honeymoon and the feeling you want, agree the fee in writing before any work begins, and see each inclusion on paper before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: The CTA comes after the evidence, which I respect, and fee and inclusions in writing are the right promises. 'The feeling you want' isn't for me. My main questions about them, how the fee works and whether they take a cut, aren't answered, so I'd email them the paid-how questions rather than book a call.

top_3_changes: Collapse the table so it doesn't pretend to compare: replace the identical 'Ask a planner' and 'Ask an agent' columns with a single 'Ask every business' column next to 'Why it matters'. No new facts needed.

In 'Where Wedded Wonderland fits', don't skip the supplier question the page told me to ask. Without adding any business fact, invite readers to put it to their Advisor as well, e.g. 'Ask your Advisor the supplier and commission questions above too, and get the answers in writing with the fee.'

Soften or cut the 'never' in 'so you never have to explain your wedding to someone who has not planned it' and add a generic reader question after the commission one: whether any supplier price includes a mark-up and whether you can see the supplier's own price.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and pricing-type sections first, looked for the catch, flagged unsupported claims
No invented brand facts; fee model, commissions, ranges, real honeymoons, insolvency cover, perks and travel support placed in unanswered_questions as deferred, not must-fix
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
Absence of figures and generalisations not treated as a must-fix; top changes require no new business facts

open_questions.question: Are the identical planner and agent columns in the table a deliberate editorial choice? If so, would a single-column version keep the 'same questions for everyone' point while avoiding the look of a comparison with no differences?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'honeymoon planner vs travel agent' while comparing three planners; relevance is 4 (on topic, useful questions, no winner declared) and enquiry likelihood is 2 because his fee and commission questions about Wedded Wonderland stay open.
Not declaring a winner and not giving figures are deliberate editorial choices; voiced as reactions but not penalised as must-fix.
The 3-minute budget covered the intro, FAQ, the table, the paid-how list, the plans-change and insurance sections and the Wedded Wonderland section, with a skim of the rest.
